source_name: Právní prostor — Novinky z oblasti práva finančních trhů
why_relevant: Second Czech legal-publishing platform carrying law-firm and academic financial-market updates (changes to the Banking Act, investment company law, capital-market rules). Complements epravo.cz and surfaces firms that do not publish there.

source_name: Lexology — Czech Republic 'What's on the horizon' / firm alerts
why_relevant: English-language syndication layer for Czech law-firm alerts; the 'What's on the horizon for 2026?' format is a ready-made forward-looking deadline tracker and a cheap way to monitor many CZ firms at once.

source_name: Mondaq — Czech Republic: Finance and Banking
why_relevant: Second syndication layer for Czech firm alerts in English; jurisdiction+topic index makes it a useful discovery feed for adviser actors not covered by epravo.cz.

source_name: ČBA EducaPlus — seminar 'Nařízení DORA a jeho dopady'
why_relevant: Czech Banking Association training arm; adviser-delivered seminars whose agendas and dates are published in Czech. Agendas act as a leading indicator of which obligations and deadlines advisers consider urgent for CZ banks, and name the practitioner speakers (actor-map fuel).

source_name: ČNB – Pravidla platebního systému CERTIS (rules page)
why_relevant: Authoritative, versioned operating rules for CERTIS issued by ČNB under §112 of Act 370/2017 Sb.; binds every CZ interbank participant and carries dated effective dates (Version 14 effective 19 May 2025 seen in results). Rule changes = dated obligations for banks and their vendors.

source_name: ČNB – CERTIS section hub (Popis systému CERTIS)
why_relevant: Hub linking rules, technical annexes, instant-payments scheme description, participant lists and the Registr pro platby na kontakt; best single snowball point for CERTIS-related obligations.

source_name: ČNB – Registr pro platby na kontakt (proxy/contact-payment register description)
why_relevant: Proxy-lookup register attached to CERTIS; its rules/technical annexes create integration obligations for participating PSPs and their core-banking vendors.

source_name: European Payments Council – SCT Inst rulebook and implementation guidelines
why_relevant: Primary scheme rulebook binding all adhering PSPs including Czech participants; carries hard dated obligations (2025 SCT Inst rulebook v1.1 in force 5 Oct 2025; unstructured address prohibited from 15 Nov 2026; change requests due 31 Dec 2025).

source_name: European Payments Council – SCT (SEPA Credit Transfer) rulebook page
why_relevant: The non-instant SCT rulebook and IGs; same structured-address and ISO 20022 migration deadlines apply to CZ PSPs handling EUR SEPA traffic.

source_name: European Payments Council – Registers of Participants (all EPC schemes)
why_relevant: Per-scheme registers (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD Core, SDD B2B, SRTP, SPAA, OCT Inst, VOP) let you enumerate which Czech PSPs have adhered to which rulebook and when — a direct, quantifiable read on CZ scheme adoption.

source_name: European Payments Council – Adhering to and using the EPC SEPA schemes (adherence process)
why_relevant: Documents the adherence procedure, cut-off dates and readiness windows a new CZ PSP must meet — the mechanism behind 'adherence deadlines' in this cell.

source_name: European Payments Council – Verification Of Payee (VoP) scheme
why_relevant: VoP rulebook in force 5 Oct 2025; euro-area PSPs had to comply by 9 Oct 2025 and non-euro-area (i.e. CZ) PSPs by 9 July 2027 for EUR instant payments — a headline dated obligation for Czech banks and their vendors, plus EPC Directory Service opt-out/billing rules.

source_name: European Payments Council – public consultations / document library
why_relevant: EPC runs formal public consultations on rulebook change requests with fixed submission windows; this is the earliest signal of upcoming dated scheme obligations affecting CZ participants.

source_name: ECB / ERPB – Status updates on SCT Inst scheme, QR-code standardisation and VoP
why_relevant: ERPB meeting documents give scheme-adoption statistics and forward timetables (including non-euro-area readiness) that EPC pages state only in prose; useful for dating obligations and gauging CZ readiness.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace – Český standard pro Open banking (COBS)
why_relevant: The Czech open-banking API standard issued by ČBA; de-facto binding on CZ banks and TPPs, released in versions (3.0/3.1/4.1/5.0/6.0, v8 referenced) with implementation windows. Core to any vendor building against CZ bank APIs.

source_name: Czech-BA/COBS GitHub repository (technical form of the Czech Open Banking Standard)
why_relevant: Machine-readable, version-tagged source of truth for COBS maintained by the ČBA working group; releases/commits give exact dates of standard changes — ideal for automated deadline tracking.

source_name: openAPI portál (apiportal.cz) – PSD2 / Czech bank API status
why_relevant: Independent CZ aggregator tracking which banks expose which API versions and PSD2 readiness; useful cross-check on COBS adoption per institution and on stragglers.

source_name: Bank iD – smluvní dokumentace (contractual documentation, incl. Service Catalogue annexes)
why_relevant: Bank iD publishes versioned, dated contractual annexes (e.g. Příloha č. 2 – Katalog služeb v10 effective 11 June 2025) plus technical specification and SLA parameters binding identity providers and relying parties — precisely the contractual-rule-with-a-deadline this cell targets.

source_name: Bank iD – Pro poskytovatele identit (rules and obligations for identity-provider banks)
why_relevant: States what each IdP bank must commit to (technical specification + SLA) to join the scheme; changes here propagate as integration obligations to banks and their vendors.

source_name: Visa – Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (public PDF)
why_relevant: The public consolidated Visa rulebook (edition dated 18 April 2026 observed) — binding on CZ acquirers, issuers and, downstream, on merchants and terminal vendors. Published on a fixed semi-annual edition cycle, so each edition is a dated obligation set.

source_name: Mastercard – Mastercard Rules (public PDF)
why_relevant: Consolidated Mastercard rulebook (edition dated 2 June 2026 observed) binding CZ licensees; source of dated mandates (e.g. the July 2026 'scam merchant' 72-hour investigation obligation reported by trade press).

source_name: Visa Czech Republic – Pravidla a předpisy platné pro karty Visa
why_relevant: Czech-language landing page pointing to the applicable Visa rules; confirms the local-language framing and gives the CZ entry point for scheme-rule references used by Czech merchants/acquirers.

source_name: ČSOB – Manuál pro obchodníky přijímající platby kartou (acquirer merchant manual)
why_relevant: Czech acquirer's merchant manual is where scheme mandates get translated into concrete local obligations and deadlines for CZ merchants and terminal estates — a practical proxy for how Visa/MC rules land in the CZ market. Comparable manuals exist at other CZ acquirers.

source_name: EPC – List of Countries in the SEPA Schemes (EPC409-09)
why_relevant: Defines the geographic scope of scheme applicability (CZ included as non-euro SEPA country) — needed to reason correctly about which EPC obligations and which timelines apply to Czech PSPs.
